hindi: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ के लिए माना कि $a_{n}=\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\binom{2n+2}{n+1}}{\binom{2n}{n}}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(a_{n}\right)^{n}$ बराबर है
solution_full: Hence $a_{n}=\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{2(2n+1)}{n+1}=\dfrac{2n+1}{2n+2}=1-\dfrac{1}{2n+2}$, which tends to $1$, while the exponent $n\to\infty$: the form is $1^{\infty}$.
For $a_{n}\to1$ and $b_{n}\to\infty$, $\lim a_{n}^{\,b_{n}}=e^{\lim b_{n}(a_{n}-1)}$ (from $\ln a_{n}\sim a_{n}-1$).
Therefore $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}(a_{n})^{n}=e^{-1/2}$. (Answering $1$ treats $1^{\infty}$ as $1$; dropping the factor $2$ in $2n+2$ gives $e^{-1}$.)
originality_note: New: the base of the 1^infinity form is the ratio of consecutive central binomial coefficients scaled by 4, which simplifies to (2n+1)/(2n+2) (way 5). Closest known: lim (1 + a/n)^n and lim ((n+a)/(n+b))^n. Different because: the base must first be produced from a binomial-coefficient ratio before the 1^infinity rule applies.

concept_use.one raise to infinity form: a_n -> 1 with exponent n; the limit is e^{lim n(a_n - 1)} = e^{-1/2}.
